strings.d1.s0.name: Fira Caldera Walking Path
strings.d1.s0.tips: Fira's caldera edge: white cubes and blue domes, with the volcano across the water.
strings.d1.s1.name: Museum of Prehistoric Thera
strings.d1.s1.tips: Akrotiri frescoes (the Blue Monkeys). Small but a must.
strings.d1.s2.name: Fira Catholic Cathedral & Streets
strings.d1.s2.tips: White-and-yellow cathedral, Gold Street shops, donkey rides.
strings.d1.s3.name: Argo Restaurant Fira
strings.d1.s4.name: Fira Cable Car & Old Port at Sunset
strings.d1.s4.tips: Take the cable car (6 EUR) down to the old port for ship lights. Return by cable car or the 588 steps.
strings.d1.b0.name: Lucky's Souvlakis Fira
strings.d1.b0.tips: Cheap gyros, instead of caldera prices.
strings.d1.b1.name: Santozeum / Megaro Gyzi
strings.d1.b1.tips: Photos of the 1956 earthquake in the Gyzi mansion; a museum alternative.
strings.d2.s0.name: Skaros Rock
strings.d2.s0.tips: 1 hour from Fira along the caldera path (set off at 07:00 in summer). A Venetian fortress rock below Imerovigli with the best views, free.
strings.d2.s1.name: Imerovigli–Oia Trail
strings.d2.s1.tips: Profitis Ilias chapel and a ridge of volcanic rock, then the descent into Oia. Carry 1.5 litres of water.
strings.d2.s2.name: Melitini Oia
strings.d2.s2.tips: Meze restaurant in Oia for lunch, with a sea-view terrace.
strings.d2.s3.name: Ammoudi Bay
strings.d2.s3.tips: Winter cove with fish tavernas (some open).
strings.d2.s4.name: Oia Castle
strings.d2.s4.tips: Ruins of the Agios Nikolaos fortress and the world-famous sunset. Grab a spot 1 hour early (or book a restaurant). Expect crowds and a bus back.
strings.d2.b0.name: Sunset Ammoudi Taverna
strings.d2.b0.tips: Grilled octopus by the bay at Ammoudi.
strings.d2.b1.name: Atlantis Books Oia
strings.d2.b1.tips: Cave-like bookshop, instead of the bay.
strings.d3.s0.name: Nea Kameni Volcano Boat
strings.d3.s0.tips: Boat from the old port (tour 30-50 EUR) to the volcanic island.
strings.d3.s1.name: Nea Kameni Crater Walk
strings.d3.s1.tips: Black lava path 130 m up to the crater, with sulphur fumes. Park fee 5 EUR.
strings.d3.s2.name: Palea Kameni Hot Springs
strings.d3.s2.tips: Jump off the boat and swim to muddy 35°C water (wear a dark swimsuit).
strings.d3.s3.name: Thirassia Island Lunch
strings.d3.s3.tips: Quiet island across the caldera. Taverna in Korfos village (if included in your tour), steps up to Manolas.
strings.d3.s4.name: Return to Oia via Ammoudi
strings.d3.s4.tips: The boat returns to Ammoudi or Fira.
strings.d3.b0.name: Catamaran Caldera Cruise
strings.d3.b0.tips: Catamaran trip to Red Beach, White Beach and the hot springs, with food and drinks included. An alternative to the volcano tour (afternoon sunset version).
strings.d3.b1.name: To Psaraki Vlychada
strings.d3.b1.tips: Fish at Vlychada harbour, if you skip the tour.
strings.d4.s0.name: Akrotiri Archaeological Site
strings.d4.s0.tips: The Minoan Pompeii of 1600 BC (three-storey houses under ash). Covered roof, go in the morning.
strings.d4.s1.name: Red Beach
strings.d4.s1.tips: A winter view of the cliffs.
strings.d4.s2.name: Akrotiri Lighthouse
strings.d4.s2.tips: 1892 lighthouse at the island's southwestern tip, with views.
strings.d4.s3.name: The Cave of Nikolas Akrotiri
strings.d4.s3.tips: Beach taverna in Akrotiri: tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters) and fava.
strings.d4.s4.name: Vlychada Beach
strings.d4.s4.tips: In winter: the tomato factory museum and white cliffs.
strings.d4.b0.name: Tomato Industrial Museum Vlychada
strings.d4.b0.tips: 1945 tomato paste factory, telling the story of Santorini's tiny tomatoes.
strings.d4.b1.name: Dolphins Akrotiri Beach Taverna
strings.d5.s0.name: Pyrgos Village & Kastelli
strings.d5.s0.tips: The island's highest village, with a Venetian castle quarter and 360° views. Few tourists.
strings.d5.s1.name: Santo Wines Pyrgos
strings.d5.s1.tips: Cooperative with caldera views. Taste Assyrtiko and Vinsanto (6 wines) with meze.
strings.d5.s2.name: Megalochori
strings.d5.s2.tips: Quiet village with a bell tower, wine cellars and a square.
strings.d5.s3.name: Venetsanos Winery
strings.d5.s3.tips: 1947 winery carved into the cliff. Go early for sunset.
strings.d5.s4.name: Domaine Sigalas Oia
strings.d5.s4.tips: In winter, Sigalas is by appointment only.
strings.d5.b0.name: Art Space Winery Exo Gonia
strings.d5.b0.tips: Art gallery in a cave winery, instead of Venetsanos.
strings.d5.b1.name: Metaxy Mas Exo Gonia
strings.d5.b1.tips: Locals' favourite taverna. Book ahead; an alternative to Santo.
strings.d6.theme: East coast beaches: Perissa and Kamari
strings.d6.s0.name: Ancient Thera
strings.d6.s0.tips: Dorian-Roman city on Mesa Vouno mountain. Zigzag road up from Kamari (taxi or scooter), with the agora and sea views.
strings.d6.s1.name: Perissa Black Beach
strings.d6.s1.tips: A winter walk on black sand.
strings.d6.s2.name: Perivolos Tranquilo Beach Bar
strings.d6.s2.tips: Sustainable beach bar serving couscous and burgers.
strings.d6.s3.name: Kamari Beach
strings.d6.s3.tips: Across from Perissa (a mountain separates them). Promenade and black pebbles, plus an open-air cinema (summer).
strings.d6.s4.name: Kamari Open Air Cinema
strings.d6.s4.tips: In winter, an evening stroll along the Kamari promenade.
strings.d6.b0.name: Monastery Kamari
strings.d6.b0.tips: Restaurant in a monastery courtyard in Kamari.
strings.d6.b1.name: Eleftherios Venizelos Museum Kamari
strings.d6.b1.tips: Small museum, a rainy-day alternative to the beach.
strings.d7.s0.name: Mezzo Imerovigli Breakfast
strings.d7.s0.tips: Breakfast with caldera views, quiet in the morning. Greek yoghurt and honey.
strings.d7.s1.name: Anastasi Church Imerovigli
strings.d7.s1.tips: Blue dome and bell. Visit after breakfast.
strings.d7.s2.name: Fira Factory Souvenirs
strings.d7.s2.tips: Vinsanto, capers, fava and volcanic stone souvenirs in Fira.
strings.d7.s3.name: Santorini Airport
strings.d7.s3.tips: From Fira: bus 20 minutes or taxi 25 EUR. Farewell (30 minutes to Athinios port for the ferry).
strings.d7.b0.name: Mama's House Fira Breakfast
strings.d7.b0.tips: Legendary cheap giant breakfast, near Fira bus station.
strings.d7.b1.name: Skaros Morning Walk
strings.d7.b1.tips: Return to the rock, instead of souvenir shopping.
strings.note0: KTEL buses run from Fira (Oia 20 min, Perissa 30 min, 2 EUR). ATV or scooter 25-40 EUR/day. Taxis are scarce (25-40 EUR). Buses serve the airport and Athinios port.
strings.note1: From November to March most hotels and restaurants are closed and it is 12-16°C; the caldera is empty, melancholy and beautiful. April-May and October are ideal (sea 20-23°C, sunset at 19:00).
strings.note2: Akrotiri 12 EUR, Thera 6, volcano tour 30-50, catamaran 120+, wine tasting 20-30. Caldera restaurants 30-50, Perissa 15-20. For tips, round up the bill.
strings.note3: Fava (yellow split pea purée), tomatokeftedes, chlorotyri cheese, white aubergine, Assyrtiko and Vinsanto. Santorini tomatoes are tiny.
strings.note4: Do the caldera hike at 07:00-08:00 (in summer). Donkey rides are available. Luggage can't be wheeled in Oia (steps), so stay in Fira or Imerovigli.
strings.note5: The hot springs stain swimsuits. Red Beach has a rockfall warning.
